# Reading and writing files

[`write_toml`](@ref) writes the site coordinates of a [`FiniteLattice`](@ref)
and the interactions of an [`OpSum`](@ref) to a TOML file. The file starts
with comments describing the lattice, followed by a `Coordinates` and an
`Interactions` array:

```toml
# This file was generated by Latlib.jl on 2026-08-13 under version "1.0.0-DEV".

# Lattice vectors: a1=(0.8660254, 0.5), a2=(0.8660254, -0.5)
# Atom positions (Cartesian basis): (0.0, 0.0), (0.57735027, -0.0)
# Atom positions (lattice basis): (0.0, 0.0), (0.33333333, 0.33333333)
# Torus vectors (Cartesian basis): t1=(0.8660254, 1.5), t2=(1.73205081, 0.0)
# Torus vectors (lattice basis): t1=(2.0, -1.0), t2=(1.0, 1.0)

Coordinates = [
  [0.0, 0.0],
  [0.8660254, 0.5],
  ...
]

Interactions = [
  ['J', 'SdotS', 0, 3],
  ['J', 'SdotS', 0, 4],
  ...
]
```

Site indices are 1-based by default; pass `zero_based=true` for 0-based
indices.

```@docs
write_toml
read_toml_interaction
```

## Helper functions

The individual sections of the TOML file can also be generated separately:

```@docs
toml_metadata
toml_lattice
toml_coordinates
toml_interactions
```
